summary_rationale: Laurus Labs has executed a credible structural pivot from an ARV-heavy generic supplier toward an innovator-led CDMO platform: CDMO reached 41.9% of H1 FY27 revenue (up 71% YoY), gross margins expanded above 60%, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin hit 33.2% (34% in Q2 FY27), USFDA compliance remained clean across Hyderabad (zero 483s) and Vizag Unit-4 (EIR) with zero adverse FDA actions through Nov 2026, manufacturing scale reached 15 sites and 8,200 KL reactor capacity, and FY26 CFO surged to Rs 1,624 Cr (182% of PAT) with Rs 560 Cr FCF. However, the business remains CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than an unconditional compounder due to structural capital intensity (cumulative FY16-FY25 FCF of only Rs 329 Cr; CWIP at Rs 1,282 Cr in Sep 2026; Rs 3,000+ Cr FY27-28 capex followed by management-guided ~Rs 1,500 Cr/yr capex beyond FY28 with peptide commercial revenues delayed until ~FY29 and slightly negative H1 FY27 FCF), 317 inventory days in FY26 (263-day cash conversion cycle), Rs 2,625 Cr of gross borrowings, a potential interest capitalization forensic flag, ongoing minority-JV outflows (Rs 107.8 Cr into 49% KRKA Pharma in Oct 2026), and geopolitical policy overhangs (2025-2026 PEPFAR/USAID funding disruptions on the 33.2% ARV base and April 2026 US Section 232 pharma tariffs incentivizing US onshoring). Governance also merits close monitoring after promoter ownership stood at a modest 27.47% (2.19% pledged) in Sep 2026 and founder-CEO Dr. Satyanarayana Chava and CFO V. V. Ravi Kumar disposed of a combined 20.7 lakh shares (~0.38% of equity) on Nov 11-12, 2026 (clarified Nov 17, 2026). KPI health remains PASS_WITH_WATCH: CDMO mix, pipeline depth (125+ projects), and >60% gross margins pass strongly, while inventory normalization, post-FY28 capex-to-ROCE conversion, and promoter alignment require ongoing monitoring.
